artboards.title: The returns card at week 6, with its why? links

annotations.text:
Chosen by the owner, 2026-09-12: A, the side drawer. Drawn on the returns card at week 6 of a real replayed game (Vella & Co., mid · lifestyle, eight keywords), with colours, type and spacing lifted from ui/style.css.

The chapter shown is the approved 'Refused at the door, or sent back', opened from the why? beside the card's legend. The other two directions are on the second page.

A · Side drawer

For: you keep your place and read the chapter beside the card it explains; the returns bars stay in view on the left. The Field guide button in the header opens the same drawer at its contents, so browsing needs no separate page.

Cost: while open it covers the right-hand column, and on a phone it has to take the whole screen.

On a phone the drawer takes the whole screen, so the card it explains is out of sight. That is why its two ways out sit in a bar pinned to the bottom: back to the card, or on to the next chapter. Every control is at least 44px tall. The chapter scrolls under the bar.

B · Unfolds in the card

For: no navigation at all. The explanation appears exactly where the question was asked.

Cost: the card grows by roughly 440px, pushing its own note below the fold and leaving the neighbouring card stranded, which is the tall-card problem the review measured. There is also nowhere to browse the other chapters.

C · Guide page

For: a calm place to read and browse every chapter, with room for longer text and a contents list.

Cost: you leave the game to read it, so the card it explains is out of sight, and 'Back to your account' has to put you back exactly where you were.
